scope: Paper/list/control objects and institutional interfaces mediating Hodgson's 1864 India Office manuscript transfer. Zoological catalogue references are explicitly separated from the manuscript-transfer chain.
central_claim: The 1864 transfer used a distributed, multilingual and hierarchical descriptive system: librarian inspection, English/Hindi contents lists, a master trunk/bundle manifest, subordinate Hindi/Nagri lists, physical bundles, and later printed/annotated manifest states.

source_control_rules: Do not treat 'the 1864 list' as one self-sufficient object; the transfer description is distributed across several control surfaces.
English/Hindi lists in Hall's hands may or may not be identical to subordinate Hindi/Nagri lists referenced in the manifest.
Summary inspection is not full cataloguing.
BHH/5/19 belongs to the zoological catalogue chain unless direct transcription disproves the present identification.
Hall's participation in two Hodgson paper networks does not merge their document ontologies.
Formal acceptance/receipt remains an open edge.
